record.title: Kulma–Karasu renewed freight closure in late 2020
record.direction: Both-direction checkpoint traffic as reported; directional volumes not verified
record.movement: Cross-border goods movements and transport businesses
record.exceptions: Post-reopening transshipment still separated national truck operations; passenger access is not established.
record.imposing_authority: Chinese authorities, as reported by Tajik sources
record.enforcement: Tajik ministry negotiations and transport-business accounts.
record.relationship: Freight-specific China-frontier phase differs from Tajik foreign-person entry regime CC012. Initial January–spring 2020 phase remains an unresolved lead.
record.status_observation: Freight handling reported restored by April 21, 2021.
record.official_rationale: Contemporary Tajik accounts attribute Chinese closure to coronavirus prevention; original Chinese order not retrieved.
record.context: Renewed episode follows earlier 2020 interruption. Restart used container transfer rather than unrestricted truck entry.
record.uncertainty: Sources are all Asia-Plus; carrier interviews and ministry statements supply different testimony but recurring chronology may be reused. End month rests on retrospective source; do not equate cargo transfer with admission of Tajik trucks.

historical.duration_note: No supported continuous operational interval for the stated scope. No measured continuous interval is established.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Carrier interviews and ministry reopening talks establish renewed disruption.

The unverified trader allegation of protectionism is not promoted to an established trade rationale. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): COVID rationale attributed to Chinese authorities; trader protectionism allegation is not verified motive.
Cargo transfer resumed; direct Tajik truck admission remained restricted.
No exact bounds or complete daily operational series.
